2609.40284.title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
2609.40284.paper_summary: Computer use agents (CUAs), which use graphical user interfaces (GUIs) to complete tasks on a computer, have recently surpassed human performance on many standard benchmarks, including difficult long-horizon tasks. Their capabilities are undoubtedly impressive, however, a key barrier to the widespread adoption and deployment of CUAs remains their speed and cost. Progress towards faster yet capable CUAs requires reliable evaluation of their speed, but many CUA benchmarks currently face a reproducibility crisis. Benchmarks are based on complex infrastructure with varying machine and container configurations that confound the evaluation of the execution speed of CUAs. Towards addressing this gap, we propose cua-speedrun, which introduces standardized infrastructure and task sets, with a focus on evaluating the speed and efficiency of CUAs. cua-speedrun uses a uniform virtual machine setup and execution pipeline, along with a common agent interface that enables single-agent implementations to operate seamlessly across different benchmarks. Across four different CUA benchmarks, we evaluate how reasoning effort, agent harnesses, and environment latency affect performance, speed, and cost. We find no single model family is optimal for all three; none of the open-weight models are on the frontier, and also, unintuitively, for some models increasing the reasoning effort can speed up task completion, while faster environment input-output can slow down overall task completion time. We also demonstrate that we can effectively reduce the evaluation task set of most CUA benchmarks without degrading overall statistical power, allowing for more efficient benchmarking and comparison. We believe cua-speedrun will enable structured progress towards fast, efficient CUAs, unlocking new real-world use cases and applications. All code, infrastructure, and analysis are available at https://cuaspeedrun.com.
2609.40284.paper_summary_zh: 電腦使用代理（CUAs）最近在許多標準基準上，包括困難的長期任務，超越了人類的表現，這些代理使用圖形用戶界面（GUIs）來完成電腦上的任務。它們的能力無疑令人印象深刻，然而，CUAs廣泛採用和部署的一個主要障礙仍然是它們的速度和成本。朝著更快但仍具能力的CUAs的進展需要可靠的速度評估，但目前許多CUA基準面臨重現性危機。基準是基於複雜的基礎設施，具有不同的機器和容器配置，這使得CUAs執行速度的評估變得困難。為了填補這一空白，我們提出了cua-speedrun，該方案引入了標準化的基礎設施和任務集，重點評估CUAs的速度和效率。cua-speedrun使用統一的虛擬機設置和執行管道，以及一個通用的代理接口，使單代理實現能夠在不同基準之間無縫運行。在四個不同的CUA基準中，我們評估了推理努力、代理工具和環境延遲如何影響性能、速度和成本。我們發現沒有任何單一模型系列對所有三者都是最佳的；沒有任何開放權重的模型處於前沿，並且，出乎意料的是，對於某些模型，增加推理努力可以加快任務完成，而更快的環境輸入輸出則可能會減慢整體任務完成時間。我們還展示了我們可以有效減少大多數CUA基準的評估任務集，而不降低整體統計能力，從而實現更高效的基準測試和比較。我們相信cua-speedrun將促進朝著快速、高效的CUAs的結構化進展，解鎖新的現實世界用例和應用。所有代碼、基礎設施和分析均可在 https://cuaspeedrun.com 獲得。
